transcript:
User: Hi. Saw your ad. Honestly I doubt this is for us but go ahead.
Agent: Gotcha, I appreciate you being straight with me — lots of folks are skeptical at first.  

So you mentioned you saw the ad… what specifically caught your eye enough to click?
User: I clicked out of curiosity; we already use an answering service but wondered if there's something better.
Agent: Got it, that makes total sense — a lot of people call us from that exact spot.  

When you say you’re wondering if there’s something better, what’s bugging you most about your current answering service right now?
User: We're actually quite satisfied with them. I doubt we need anything additional or different at this point.
Agent: Totally fair, if you’re happy I’m not here to twist your arm.  

Just so I don’t waste your time — if your answering service ever drops a call or can’t book something, what typically happens to that customer?
User: Occasionally, we miss about 10 calls a week. Not ideal, but we manage. Convince me you do better.
Agent: Makes sense — you’re managing, but 10 a week is still 10 people you never talk to.  

So when those 10 calls don’t get picked up live, do they usually leave a voicemail, call back later, or just disappear to someone else?
User: Some leave voicemails, but I suspect many just move on. Convince me this service is worth considering.
Agent: Right, so you’re basically paying to generate calls… and then watching a slice of them vanish.  

Has anyone ever actually walked you through what those 10 missed calls a week might be costing you in real dollars?
User: No one's broken it down exactly. But let's cut to the chase: what's this going to cost? Give me a number.
Agent: Totally hear you, you want to know if this is even in the right ballpark before anything else.  

Before we talk dollars though, can I get a quick sense of what each booked job is worth to you on average — are we talking more like a $200 job, $500, $1,000?
User: Our average value per booked patient is around $700. But seriously, what's your pricing range?
Agent: Perfect, $700 helps a lot.  

If you’re missing about 10 calls a week and even half of those would’ve booked, that’s roughly $3,500 a week walking out the door — and over a month, about $15,100. Does that feel in the realm of realistic for your clinic, or high/low?
User: That sounds about right, but enough dodging. What's this going to cost us? Give me a number.
Agent: Totally get it, you want a straight answer.  

Here’s how we handle it: pricing depends on your call flow and setup, and Jay walks through exact numbers on a quick live call — if I could guarantee you 5–10 extra booked patients a month, would it be worth 20 minutes this week to see the math and the actual price?
User: If you can assure me this isn't a sketchy startup disappearing with our data, I'll consider it.
Agent: Yeah, that’s a totally fair concern — you don’t want to be a guinea pig with patient data on the line.  

When you say “not disappearing with our data,” is your bigger worry more about HIPAA / data security, or about whether we’re a stable, long-term partner?
User: Both, really. I need solid data security assurances and to know you're not vanishing in a year.
Agent: Got it, both security and staying power matter, especially in healthcare.  

So… it’s a 20‑minute walkthrough where Jay can show you exactly how we handle data, compliance, and what those missed calls look like in real numbers for your clinic — what’s better for you this week, later today or tomorrow?
User: How do I know this isn't some sketchy startup that disappears with our patient data? Convince me first.
Agent: Totally fair — with patient data, “trust us” isn’t good enough.  

On the security side, we use healthcare‑grade encryption (in transit and at rest), data lives on hardened cloud infrastructure, and access is tightly permissioned — and you control what we can and can’t touch.  

On the “not vanishing” side, we’re not trying to be everything to everyone — we’re focused on clinics exactly like yours that are bleeding revenue on missed calls, and we only win if we stay in place and keep booking patients for you month after month.  

Given you’re losing around $15k a month on missed calls, is it reasonable to at least see how we’d handle your call flow and data on a 20‑minute walkthrough with Jay this week — later today or tomorrow?
User: Alright, but I tried AI last year, it was garbage and wasted three months. Why is yours different?
Agent: Yeah, I hear you — if you burned three months on bad AI, you’re not eager to repeat that.  

What specifically made it “garbage” for you — was it saying dumb things to patients, not actually booking, or just impossible to set up and manage?
User: It was clunky to set up, didn't understand our patients, and failed to book appointments reliably.
Agent: Yeah, that’s exactly the kind of experience we hear about, and it’s brutal when it’s with your patients.  

So the big differences with what we do are: we plug into your existing booking flow so it actually books, it’s trained around medical-style conversations so it understands what people are asking, and we stay on top of it with real call reviews instead of “set it and forget it.”  

Given that, and knowing you’re leaking around $15k a month on missed calls, is it worth 20 minutes this week for Jay to walk you through how this would handle your real patient calls and bookings—later today or tomorrow?
User: Okay, let's book a call for tomorrow afternoon. Can you confirm the time and details?
Agent: Awesome, tomorrow afternoon works.  

First thing I’ll do is grab some quick details so we can lock it in properly — what’s your first name?
User: It's Brenda. Make sure to use my corrected number, +16025550017, when you call. Looking forward to it.
Agent: Nice to meet you, Brenda.  

Got your number noted — and just to finish locking this in, what’s the name of your company or clinic?
User: Desert Bloom Dental, based in Phoenix, Arizona. Looking forward to tomorrow's call.
Agent: Got it, Desert Bloom Dental in Phoenix — sounds great.  

Closest “tomorrow afternoon” I can get you is actually this Thursday; I can do Thursday at 1:45 or 2:30 Central (11:45 or 12:30 your time in Phoenix) — which works better for you?
User: Let's go with Thursday at 12:30 Arizona time. Please use +16025550017 to reach me. Confirm, please.
Agent: One moment while I confirm that.
Agent: Brenda, you’re all set for Thursday at 12:30 your time in Arizona, and we’ll call you at +1 602 555 0017. You’ll get a text with the confirmation details shortly — you can add it to your calendar or reschedule from there if anything changes.

Is there anything else you need from me before we hop off?

Alright, really glad we got this set up. Jay’s looking forward to meeting you and digging into those missed calls for Desert Bloom Dental. Have a great rest of your day — bye for now!
